conditions: HTTP request with regular browser user agent

findings.summary: No user-preference-driven dark theme
findings.evidence: The dark/reduce/contrast screenshot is visually identical to the light screenshot: white content surfaces and the fixed blue chrome do not retint.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() for text, surfaces, borders, and browser chrome.

findings.summary: High-contrast usability is not preserved
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 191 color-contrast failures, and the prefers-contrast: more capture does not increase contrast or otherwise adapt controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Meet WCAG contrast minimums and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast treatments for controls and custom chrome.

findings.summary: Route and state changes swap abruptly
findings.evidence: CDP CSS inspection found no view-transition rules across the homepage and four route archetypes; navigation uses immediate document/hash swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance same-document tabs and cross-document routes with View Transitions, retaining an instant fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome does not respond to scroll position
findings.evidence: Long listing pages reach thousands of pixels, but CDP inspection and screenshots show static/fixed chrome with no scroll-state feedback or progress cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Use declarative scroll-state/container queries or a lightweight progress affordance where it helps orientation.

findings.summary: Large ad slots and dense application chrome crowd the content
findings.evidence: The first desktop viewport reserves roughly 170px of blank advertising space before the search/list, while mobile devotes much of the first screen to login, ad, tabs, controls, and fixed navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Collapse empty ad inventory, reserve only occupied ad space, and simplify repeated tab/chrome treatments around the primary listing.

findings.summary: Many targets are too small and focus is inconsistent
findings.evidence: The mobile CDP probe found 38 controls below 24px in at least one dimension on home and 44 on popular; focused search controls had outline-width 0 while only some anchors retained the UA outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 24x24 CSS px targets (prefer 44px for primary touch controls), spacing, and a strong :focus-visible style.

findings.summary: Failure states do not explain recovery
findings.evidence: A request to an unknown route returns a bare “404 Not Found” response with no site navigation, search, retry, or route back to the primary task.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a branded 404/error state with search, home/popular links, and clear recovery actions; preserve context for in-app failures.

findings.summary: Largest content appears too late
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured FCP and LCP at 4.35s (performance 0.73), outside the 2.5s good LCP range, although CLS and TBT were good.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content, shorten render-blocking chains, and verify LCP under representative mobile network conditions.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and cache policy delay content
findings.evidence: Lighthouse identified 11 render-blocking resources with about 2.36s estimated savings, inefficient cache lifetimes, font-display delay, and a 42-request/521KiB load.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, inline or preload only critical styles/fonts, set durable cache headers on versioned assets, and preserve text during font loading.

findings.summary: The page ships avoidable unused CSS and JavaScript
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 48KiB unused CSS and 59KiB unused JavaScript on the homepage, alongside old general-purpose UI libraries.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unused Bootstrap/jQuery UI surface area or split it by template; load only code needed for the current route.

findings.summary: Forms, frames, and media lack complete accessible names
findings.evidence: The CDP probe found the primary search text input and actress/password fields without labels; Lighthouse also reports five untitled iframes, an unnamed link, and invalid ARIA-required children.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit labels and autocomplete, title every iframe, repair role ownership, and give meaningful linked images/controls accessible names.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI fail contrast requirements
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 191 failing color-contrast nodes across the dense listing UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to WCAG AA contrast and verify normal, hover, focus, disabled, and high-contrast states.

findings.summary: Heading, landmark, and focus structure is incomplete
findings.evidence: All five templates have zero <main> landmarks and start visible content at H3; Lighthouse reports heading-order and list-item structure failures, while several controls suppress focus outlines.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark, restore a logical H1→H2 hierarchy, valid list semantics, and visible focus order.

findings.summary: Dense small text reduces reading comfort
findings.evidence: Mobile screenshots show crowded 14px tags, tightly packed explanatory copy, and multiple rows of controls/content in narrow cards.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase base/secondary text sizes and line-height, reduce simultaneous metadata, and use wrapping/spacing that preserves scannability.

findings.summary: Touch and embedded-media accessibility is incomplete
findings.evidence: Although all templates reflow without horizontal overflow and permit scaling, dozens of controls are under 24px and Lighthouse reports five iframes without titles.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target size and spacing, title embedded frames, and verify captions/equivalents for each media provider.

findings.summary: A production asset fails to load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse logged net::ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED for a do-gasource.eroterest.net WebP resource.
findings.suggestedFix: Fix or remove the failing resource URL and add a resilient image fallback.

findings.summary: Image sizing and document structure are unsound
findings.evidence: CDP found one or two images per audited template without width/height attributes; Lighthouse also reports malformed list/ARIA structure.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic image width/height or aspect-ratio and repair invalid list/role structures.

findings.summary: Stale dependencies and cache policy weaken platform hygiene
findings.evidence: Rendered markup loads jQuery 3.4.1, jQuery UI 1.12.1, Bootstrap 4.4.1, and touch-punch 0.2.3; Lighthouse reports inspector issues and three BFCache blockers caused by no-store/cookie mutation.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or remove stale libraries, resolve DevTools issues, and avoid no-store on public listing pages so BFCache can work.

findings.summary: Canonical and sitemap signals are missing
findings.evidence: All public templates return 200 and index,follow but expose no canonical URL; /sitemap.xml returns 404 while robots.txt is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Publish canonical links per indexable template and a sitemap consistent with robots/indexing policy.

findings.summary: Public entities lack structured and social metadata
findings.evidence: The homepage raw HTML contains no JSON-LD/microdata, Open Graph, or Twitter Card metadata despite representing searchable video entities.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate schema.org collection/video metadata where supportable plus Open Graph/Twitter preview tags matching visible content.

findings.summary: Session and persistent identifiers lack cookie protections
findings.evidence: The 200 response sets PHPSESSID, uidhash, and uidhash3 without Secure, HttpOnly, or SameSite; PHPSESSID is retained for roughly five years and identifiers for roughly six years.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark session cookies Secure, HttpOnly, and SameSite=Lax/Strict as appropriate; use short session expiry and rotate identifiers.

findings.summary: Persistent identifiers and third parties load without minimisation evidence
findings.evidence: Every audited template contacts nine third-party origins, and the site creates multi-year uidhash identifiers plus localStorage synchronization during initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove unnecessary identity storage, shorten retention, gate non-essential third parties on consent, and batch/minimise analytics.

findings.summary: Authentication relies on an unlabeled passphrase field
findings.evidence: The account entry route offers only a password/passphrase input with no label, autocomplete token, required state, or WebAuthn/passkey alternative; no permission prompt fired on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Label the field, add current-password autocomplete, and offer passkeys/WebAuthn with password fallback and in-context prompts.

findings.summary: Core browser-enforced defenses are absent
findings.evidence: The successful document response has no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy response header, or Permissions-Policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, a nonce/hash CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, strict referrer policy, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: HTTP failure handling collapses to a dead end
findings.evidence: The representative 404 response is plain text only, with no navigation, search, retry, or explanation.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve resilient error templates with recovery links and retain the global task/navigation shell.

findings.summary: Advertising is visually blended with result content
findings.evidence: The first desktop result grid begins with a promotional card using the same image/card placement and red headline treatment as content, without a clear ad label; large ad slots also precede results.
findings.suggestedFix: Clearly label advertising, visually separate it from organic results, and keep promotions from imitating result cards.

findings.summary: Forms lack native validation and accessible feedback hooks
findings.evidence: The login passphrase and actress/search text controls are unlabeled and required=false; no aria-invalid/error-announcement structure was found in the rendered form states.
findings.suggestedFix: Use labels and required constraints, validate after interaction with :user-invalid, and announce actionable errors accessibly.

findings.summary: Input fields omit autocomplete assistance
findings.evidence: The login passphrase, search, and actress-name fields all expose an empty autocomplete value.
findings.suggestedFix: Add current-password to login and appropriate search/name autocomplete tokens; preserve password-manager compatibility.

findings.summary: Account entry lacks modern, proportionate authentication support
findings.evidence: The only observed account-entry method is a passphrase field, with no passkey, recovery, or reauthentication affordance visible on the representative login route.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkeys with clear fallback/recovery and proportionate reauthentication for sensitive account actions.

findings.summary: Images are not responsively delivered
findings.evidence: Homepage/list templates serve 32–54 images with no srcset in the sampled DOM; Lighthouse estimates image-delivery savings and CDP found missing intrinsic dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP responsive srcsets/sizes, keep lazy loading below fold, and set intrinsic dimensions.

findings.summary: Third-party and embedded-media cost is high for the first view
findings.evidence: The homepage loads 42 requests/521KiB and five iframes across nine third-party origins before the user selects a result.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load embeds/ads behind user intent or viewport proximity and enforce per-template third-party budgets.

Remove render-blocking work and prioritize LCP

Make forms humane and add passkey-ready account entry
Separate ads from results and reduce first-viewport chrome
Add canonical, sitemap, structured data, and social previews
Add preference-driven theme and progressive transitions
Improve text density and reading comfort
